label: External cause outside the caused…: A1c2 invokes 'external' so that an external cause of C is…
term: external cause outside the caused thing and its parts (A1c2)
definition: A1c2 invokes 'external' so that an external cause of C is distinct from C and every part of C. The label alone does not show that any cause exists, nor that the universal external-cause law holds for all contingent things.
note: The Lean interpretation exposes the full exclusion clause for a particular cause and selected thing on an arbitrary carrier: cause c whole ∧ c ≠ whole ∧ ∀ p, part p whole → c ≠ p. Cause and part are explicit primitive relation parameters, without imposed structural laws; they are not definitions of productive causation or parthood. No world, time, actual existence, concreteness, nonoverlap or necessity is inferred. Reflexive and proper parthood are both admitted because self-exclusion is explicit. General applicability of these relations and identification with Scenario Causes and Mathlib parthood remain open. Bool examples are controls only; no finite restriction is imposed on the definition. The source claim is unchanged; this declaration interprets its exclusion gloss, not its universal contingent-cause principle.
